entries.title: Psalms 32:2
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Imputeth - Whom God doth not charge with the guilt of his sins, but graciously pardons and accepts him in Christ. No guile - Who freely confesses all his sins, and turns from sin to God with all his heart.

entries.title: Psalms 32:3
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Silence - From a full and open confession of my sins. Old - My spirit failed, and the strength of my body decayed. Roaring - Because of the continual horrors of my conscience, and sense of God's wrath.

entries.title: Psalms 32:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Hand - Thy afflicting hand. My moisture - Was dried up.

entries.title: Psalms 32:5
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The iniquity - The guilt of my sin.

entries.title: Psalms 32:6
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: For this - Upon the encouragement of my example. Found - In an acceptable and seasonable time, while God continues to offer grace and mercy. Waters - In the time of great calamities. Not come - So as to overwhelm him.

entries.title: Psalms 32:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: I will - This and the next verse seems to be the words of God, whom David brings in as returning this answer to his prayers. Mine eye - So Christ did St. Peter, when he turned and looked upon him.

entries.title: Psalms 32:9
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Will not - Unless they be forced to it by a bit or bridle. And so all the ancient translators understand it.

entries.title: Psalms 32:10
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Sorrows - This is an argument to enforce the foregoing admonition.
